title: 'My Crash Was So Unlikely' - Lindsey Vonn Shares Raw Truth About Moment That 'Overshadowed' Her Comeback Story - NewsBreak
text:
By Adityan Pillai ,
1 hours ago
[US, Mexico & Canada customers only] Feb 3, 2026; Cortina d'Ampezzo, ITALY; Lindsey Vonn attends a press conference at a press conference at the Cortina Curling Olympic Stadium in preparation for the Milano Cortina 2026 Olympic Winter Games. Mandatory Credit: Leonhard Foeger/Reuters via Imagn Images
Lindsey Vonn opened up about the moment that completely changed her comeback journey. She keeps going back to what it felt like at the start—that brief stretch where everything was in place and she knew what she could do.
The American athlete expressed how the tragic crash completely changed the trajectory of what could have been a successful comeback story. Lindsey Vonn opened up about the moment she began the race despite dealing with an ACL issue during the Olympics, speaking in an interview with ESPN. She focused on what it took just to get to that start line again.
What Changed for Lindsey Vonn During Her Olympic Comeback It wasn’t about proving anything to anyone. For her, it came down to being there, ready to go, even with everything she had been dealing with behind the scenes. She then walked through what those first seconds actually felt like once the race began—not the outcome, but the feeling of being in control, knowing the course, and trusting herself in that moment.
That’s when she paused and got into the part that still surprises her: how something so small ended up changing everything.
“I mean, I was fully in control until I hit that panel, to be honest. I was in such a good mental state. Despite my ACL, I was physically in a great place. I felt strong. I know that course like the back of my hand. I know exactly what to do. My crash was so unlikely and improbable and something I would have never in a million years guessed would happen. But those are the margins that you’re playing with in downhill,” she said .
She went on to explain what that moment meant to her before the race even started. It wasn’t about how far she would go down the course, but about the belief she had standing there and what it took to reach that point again.
MORE: Lindsey Vonn’s Unbreakable Mental Toughness Forged Through Family Sacrifice and Personal Tragedy, Expert Reveals
The American athlete expressed how the bigger picture got lost and how everything she had worked toward in the past year and a half ended up being overshadowed by that one moment.
“I stood in the starting gate knowing that I could win the race, and that was the only medal that I was looking forward to. I didn’t make it very far, but I actually made it really far because I was 41 years old with a partial knee replacement and no ACL. And the fact that I was there was a huge victory in itself. And I think everyone’s been so focused on the crash that the overall story has been somewhat overshadowed by it,” she concluded.
READ MORE: Lindsey Vonn Sends Rumor Mill Into Overdrive By Teasing Another Uphill Comeback
Vonn is still working her way back, and it’s not a straight path. Recovery has been slow, with time spent rehabbing and getting strength back step by step.
Even now, she hasn’t ruled anything out. She’s taking it day by day, focusing on getting better first. What comes after that is still open, and she seems fine leaving it that way for now.
